2610.12304.title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance
2610.12304.paper_summary: Understanding large language model (LLM) reasoning requires looking beyond behavioral performance to examine how reasoning ability is reflected in internal organization. Inspired by neuroscience findings linking higher intelligence to stronger small-world organization in functional brain networks, we investigate small-world connectivity as a structural signature of LLM reasoning. We construct functional graphs from attention-head activation similarities and find that a higher small-world index (SWI), capturing local clustering and short global paths, consistently correlates with better fluid reasoning performance across models and training checkpoints. Since local clustering is central to small-world organization, we further examine how heads important for model performance connect within and across communities. We find that these heads tend to have a larger share of connection weight within their own communities (high core scores) and a more concentrated weight distribution across communities (low bridge scores). These observations motivate the hypothesis that high core and low bridge scores serve as structural indicators of head importance for reasoning capability. We validate this hypothesis through pruning, introducing Small-World Allocation (SWA), a hierarchical sparsity allocation method guided by these scores. Across six LLMs, SWA better preserves small-world organization and model performance than competing allocation strategies, reducing WikiText perplexity by up to 20%. Together, these findings identify small-world functional connectivity as a measurable signature of LLM reasoning performance, offering a structural perspective that complements behavioral evaluation.
2610.12304.paper_summary_zh: 理解大型語言模型（LLM）推理需要超越行為表現，檢視推理能力如何在內部組織中反映出來。受到神經科學研究的啟發，該研究將更高的智力與功能性大腦網絡中的強小世界組織聯繫起來，我們調查小世界連通性作為LLM推理的結構特徵。我們從注意力頭的激活相似性構建功能圖，發現較高的小世界指數（SWI），捕捉局部聚類和短的全局路徑，與模型和訓練檢查點之間的流暢推理表現持續相關。由於局部聚類是小世界組織的核心，我們進一步檢查對模型性能重要的頭部在社群內部和社群之間的連接方式。我們發現這些頭部在其自身社群內的連接權重佔比更大（高核心分數），而在社群之間的權重分佈則更集中（低橋樑分數）。這些觀察促使我們提出假設：高核心分數和低橋樑分數作為推理能力的重要性結構指標。我們通過修剪來驗證這一假設，推出小世界分配（SWA），這是一種基於這些分數的分層稀疏分配方法。在六個LLM中，SWA比競爭的分配策略更好地保留了小世界組織和模型性能，將WikiText困惑度降低了多達20%。總的來說，這些發現將小世界功能連通性確定為LLM推理性能的可測量特徵，提供了一種補充行為評估的結構視角。
